letters.title: Institutional letter of support
letters.use: From a Yale leader (for example a center or institute director) backing the project and the team.
letters.body:
[Date]

[Funder name]
[Program or call name]

Dear Review Committee,

I am writing to express [my / the institute's] strong support for the proposal "[Project title]", led by [PI name, title, department] at Yale University.

[One or two sentences on why the project matters and how it fits the institute's priorities.]

[PI name] and the team bring [key strengths: expertise, prior work, partnerships]. The project builds on [existing collaboration or work, if any] with [partner institution(s), country].

[If true and approved: describe the specific support being offered, such as staff time, space, access to resources, or other commitments. Leave this out unless it has been agreed.]

I am pleased to support this proposal and look forward to its success.

Sincerely,

[Name]
[Title]
[Unit], Yale University

letters.title: Letter from a partner institution
letters.use: A collaborating organization confirms its role. Send it to the partner to adapt and put on their letterhead.
letters.body:
[Partner letterhead]

[Date]

Dear [PI name],

On behalf of [partner organization], I am pleased to confirm our commitment to collaborate on "[Project title]", submitted to [funder / program].

As part of this project, [partner organization] will [describe the agreed role: e.g. lead recruitment at the study site, provide laboratory access, co-supervise trainees].

[Optional: a sentence on the history of the collaboration.]

[Optional and only if agreed: resources the partner will contribute.]

We look forward to working with you and the Yale team.

Sincerely,

[Name]
[Title]
[Organization], [Country]

letters.title: Letter from a collaborating Yale faculty member
letters.use: A co-investigator or consultant confirms what they will contribute.
letters.body:
[Date]

Dear [PI name],

I am happy to take part in "[Project title]" as [role: co-investigator / consultant / mentor].

I will contribute [specific expertise or tasks] and expect to commit [effort, if agreed] to the project.

[One sentence on relevant experience.]

I look forward to working with you.

Sincerely,

[Name]
[Title, Department]
Yale University

checklists.title: Before you start a proposal with an international partner
items: Read the full call and note the sponsor deadline and any internal Yale deadlines.
Tell your department grants administrator early.
Confirm each partner can receive funds and has the registrations the funder asks for.
Check whether the partner country raises export control or research security questions.
Plan the ethics review: Yale IRB and any local ethics committee.
Ask for letters of support early; leaders and partners need time.
Draft the budget with costs at the international site, including subawards.

checklists.title: When asking for a letter of support
items: Give at least two to three weeks' notice.
Send the call, the deadline and a short summary of the project.
Say exactly what the letter should confirm, and only ask for commitments that have been agreed.
Offer a draft the signer can edit.
Say how it should be sent back (signed PDF, letterhead) and to whom.

checklists.title: Before traveling for research
items: Register your trip with Yale's travel resources.
Check travel advisories for the country.
Check whether laptops, equipment or samples need export review.
Confirm ethics approvals cover the work you will do there.
Carry contact details for your in-country partner and Yale's emergency support.

checklists.title: Before hosting an international visitor
items: Agree on the purpose, length and activities of the visit.
Start the visa and appointment process with the right office well ahead of time.
Check research security guidance, especially for countries of concern.
Arrange access to space, systems and any required training.
Plan how the visit will be funded and what costs are covered.
